hints: Look closely at the bonding in nitrogen and at what really happens when ammonia dissolves in water, not just the formula on the bottle.
Recall that $N_2$ has a very strong triple bond with a lone pair on each N, and that $NH_3(aq)$ sets up an equilibrium with water to give $NH_4^+(aq)$ and $OH^-(aq)$.
Apply the Bronsted-Lowry definition of a proton donor to $NH_4^+(aq)$, and remember photochemical smog comes from nitrogen oxides with hydrocarbons, not $SO_2$.
walkthrough:
**Check the structure of nitrogen**

Nitrogen exists as $N_2$ with a very strong triple bond, $N \equiv N$. Each nitrogen atom still has one lone pair.

Its unreactivity is due to the huge bond energy needed to break the triple bond, not due to missing lone pairs:
$$N \equiv N \text{ (bond energy } \approx 945 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1})$$

**Check what is in aqueous ammonia**

When ammonia dissolves, it acts as a weak base and establishes an equilibrium with water. Both the molecule and its conjugate acid are present.

$$NH_3(aq) + H_2O(l) \rightleftharpoons NH_4^+(aq) + OH^-(aq)$$

**Apply the Bronsted-Lowry definition**

A Bronsted-Lowry acid is a proton ($H^+$) donor. A Bronsted-Lowry base is a proton acceptor.

$$NH_4^+(aq) \rightarrow NH_3(aq) + H^+(aq)$$
Since $NH_4^+$ can donate a proton to become $NH_3$, it fits the definition of a Bronsted-Lowry acid perfectly.

**Eliminate the other statements**

High temperature is needed to break a triple bond in $N_2$, not a double bond. Photochemical smog forms from $NO_x$ and unburnt hydrocarbons in sunlight, while $SO_2$ causes acid rain, not photochemical smog. So only the ammonia statement is fully correct.

options.A: Incorrect. $N_2$ does have lone pairs, one on each N atom ($:N \equiv N:$). Its low reactivity is due to the very high bond dissociation energy of the $N \equiv N$ triple bond, which requires a lot of energy to break.
options.B: Correct. Aqueous ammonia is a weak base equilibrium containing mainly $NH_3(aq)$ with some $NH_4^+(aq)$ and $OH^-(aq)$. The $NH_4^+$ ion can donate a proton to form $NH_3$, so it is the conjugate acid and a Bronsted-Lowry acid.
options.C: Incorrect. Nitrogen molecules contain a strong triple bond, not a double bond. High temperatures, for example in car engines or lightning, are needed to provide the activation energy to break this $N \equiv N$ triple bond to form nitrogen oxides.
options.D: Incorrect. Photochemical smog is formed by the reaction of nitrogen oxides ($NO_x$) with unburnt hydrocarbons in sunlight, forming ozone and PAN. Atmospheric $SO_2$ leads to acid rain and sulfurous smog, not photochemical smog.
